summary: Anthropic reports that US-government export controls applied to Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 on June 12 have been lifted as of June 30, restoring global access to Fable 5 and partial access to Mythos 5, alongside new safety classifiers, a proposed cross-industry jailbreak severity framework, and expanded government collaboration commitments.

mechanisms.reason: The document describes the US government both applying export controls to two named frontier models and then lifting them weeks later, directly restricting and then restoring model access.
mechanisms.quote: On Friday, June 12, the US government applied export controls to our newest models, Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5.

mechanisms.reason: Access to a suspended frontier model is being restored globally across multiple surfaces, reversing an earlier volume-negative suspension.
mechanisms.quote: Access to Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 is now restored.

practices.reason: The proposed four-criteria jailbreak severity framework gives security and safety teams a concrete method to triage and score jailbreak findings, though it is explicitly a work in progress.
practices.quote: Our current proposal is to score a given jailbreak on the four different criteria below.

practices.reason: Usage-limit allowances change on a fixed date and blocked requests are automatically rerouted to a different model, both of which require integration and monitoring updates for any team building on Fable 5.
practices.quote: Users will be notified if a request to Fable 5 is blocked, and the request will instead be sent to Opus 4.8.

notable_reason: This is a rare disclosed case of US export controls being applied directly to a frontier model's access and then lifted, accompanied by a new cross-industry jailbreak severity framework with Amazon, Microsoft and Google.
